no_lantern.text: Hm. A lamplighter without a lantern is like a smith without a hammer. Go to Oldrich, he's waiting for you. Been pacing by his door for three days.

text: Hm. So Oldrich gave you his father's lantern after all. Let me see.
Good work. Old. The tank is small, the cap is burnt through. It'll get you up the hill, but beyond that — I don't know.

choices.text: It served forty years. It'll serve more.

stubborn.text: Stubborn. That's good. Stubbornness is the same as patience, only with fists. But listen anyway.

offer.text: Bring me copper — wire, even one coil. I'll make a bigger tank and a sturdier cap. It'll burn longer and shine wider. Mara has copper sometimes… she trades. Tell her it's for me — she'll… no, don't tell her.

waiting.text: Brought the copper? No? Well, the anvil can wait. It's patient — it's been beaten for twenty years and it still stands.

forge.text: Now that's more like it! Sit, I'll be quick. The fire in my forge never goes out — I didn't put it out even under the decree. Kept it quiet, under the ash.

choices.text: Why didn't you put it out?

why.text: Why would I? Fire is like hope. You don't hold it in a fist — you'll smother it. You keep it in your palms. Quietly, but you keep it.

work.text: Done. Tank twice as big, copper cap. Here. And don't play the hero — the lantern is new, but your legs are old.

done.text: Well, does it shine? There you go. For twenty years I hammered the anvil so I wouldn't hear the silence. Today I hammered it because there was someone to hammer for.

after.text: Hear how it rings? I used to strike to drown out the silence. Now I strike so it can be heard. Feel the difference? So do I, now.

text: Eh? My hands? Nothing wrong with my hands. So I burned them. A smith without burns is no smith.

…Fine. They hurt. I can hold a hammer, but not a nail. Vale in the forest makes a salve that heals it in a week. Only he needs moonwort, and I haven't gone near the forest in — well, you know how many years.

choices.text: I'll gather the herb and go to Vale.

burn_why.text: Because a smith doesn't complain. Horseshoes complain to him. Go on, since you noticed. The herb glows blue — in open places, where the wind blows.

burn_ok.text: Four stalks, Vale said. It glows blue and grows where it's open and windy. Thank you, old man.

text: Salve? From Vale? Let's see… Oh. It's cold. Like snow down your collar, only nice.
Listen. While my hands were healing — well, while you were walking — I thought something up for you. A hood for the lantern. Copper, with slits: the wind goes around it, and the flame can breathe.
Give me the lantern. …There. Now the Pall can blow all it likes — your fire will hardly notice.
A letter for me? Who'd write to me… Ha! It's Yarik, my apprentice! Ran off to the city, the rascal, twenty years ago.

"Master, I'm a smith myself now, with my own forge and two apprentices. I teach them the way you taught me: iron doesn't like hurry. When it's light in the Ford, I'll come and show you what I've forged."
Iron doesn't like hurry… He remembers, eh. Here, take some oil. Take it, take it, I'm kind today.
